items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: They had Bert Sigerson from New Orleans... But anyway, they had always wanted me to join them... I preferred to play one-nighters... But they finally taught me into joining the band

ctx.x: I didn't get what he played. Well, actually, this was just a little trio.

And, it was Jack and Terry Sheehan up in, uh, Thomas John, and William Gramsson, and all that stuff. And, they played all the society dances, and they played the Fiori roof garden. And, this particular man, this guy, who I was talking about, uh, was, uh, Asian. He hired them. And, uh, so I guess the buddies then, uh, who, uh, who, uh, were, uh, uh, who, uh, were included the Red Round Tree and Buddy Seeky and drums and, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um,…
No, that's right. You didn't tell me much about New Orleans, you tripped down.

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Burt Sigerson' as a member of a previous band ('the first band they had, uh, consisted of this Burt Sigerson...') but does not describe a personal interaction or relationship with him, only his membership in the group.

ctx.x: Dick Coleman was, uh, a banjo player. Wow. And a vocalist, and he was very good. He was, uh, he went to the University of Alabama. He was a Kappa Alpha. And extremely popular with the ladies. Uh-huh. And, uh, so he was, uh, one of the original members of the Brothers Brumelty Boys, also. See, this thing went through so many changes. I, uh, the original Brothers Brumelty Boys, uh, Pruitt and Dick Coleman were both in that band. Uh-huh. And, uh, Dick, uh, he was with a lot of different bands. And, uh, he and Pruitt…
Well, uh, we won't, maybe we can do another reel, huh? Uh-huh. And talk, talk about Mississippi musicians. Of course, I want to talk about a lot of people. I don't know where Bert Sigerson is now.
